title: Unfu*k Yourself
short_description: Bishop’s tough-love assertiveness — stop self-talk spirals, claim responsibility, and act before you feel ready.

questions.question_text: What does Bishop emphasize about self-talk?
questions.option_b: Assertive language plus action can interrupt stuck spirals
Act within safety before you feel ready — feelings often follow

questions.option_a: Demand total certainty before any step
questions.option_b: Tolerate not knowing while taking small reviewed bets
Taking responsibility for responses in health, money, relationships, craft
Productive discomfort beyond old self-stories — with recovery

title: Ego Is the Enemy
short_description: Ryan Holiday on how ego sabotages aspiration, success, and failure — and how humility and reality keep you growing.
chapter_titles: Chapter 1: Ego as the invisible opponent
Chapter 4: Live with purpose, not passion theater
Chapter 6: The peril of branding yourself
Chapter 8: Dead time vs alive time

questions.question_text: What does Holiday treat as the real enemy?
questions.option_b: Ego — an unhealthy belief in your own importance
Help others succeed while you learn and build skill
Using delays and constraints to train and improve

questions.question_text: Why is success dangerous in this book?
questions.option_b: Wins can inflate ego and stop learning

questions.question_text: What stance does Holiday recommend for life?
questions.option_b: Remain a student so ego cannot declare you finished

title: Feel the Fear and Do It Anyway
short_description: Susan Jeffers on moving through fear — the fear will never fully go away, but you can act anyway.
chapter_titles: Chapter 2: The three levels of fear
Chapter 3: The fear will never go away as long as you grow
Chapter 4: How you talk to yourself matters
Chapter 6: Say yes to your bigger life
Chapter 12: Do it anyway as a life stance

questions.question_text: According to Jeffers, when does fear go away?
questions.option_a: As soon as you become successful
questions.option_b: Fear does not fully go away if you keep growing — you learn to act anyway

questions.question_text: What is the deepest level of fear in Jeffers’ model?
questions.option_b: Fear that you cannot handle whatever happens

questions.question_text: What is the no-lose decision idea?
questions.option_b: Any chosen path can produce growth if you commit and learn
questions.option_c: Only one path is ever correct

questions.question_text: How should you treat fear while growing?
questions.option_b: As a companion signal — act while afraid when values say go
questions.option_d: As something only weak people feel

questions.question_text: What does taking responsibility mean here?
questions.option_b: Owning your responses and agency without erasing real limits
